title: JSON Encoding & Basic HTTP
intro: JSON and basic HTTP are the two standard library features every Go fresher uses on day one. This module covers encoding/json for serialisation (json.Marshal a struct → JSON bytes, json.Unmarshal JSON bytes → struct), struct tags for controlling JSON field names (json:"field_name" and json:"field,omitempty" to omit zero values), common gotchas (unexported fields are silently ignored, json.Number for avoiding float64 precision loss on large integers, map[string]interface{} as the catch-all for unknown JSON), the net/http client for making HTTP requests (http.Get, http.Post, the critical must-close-response-body pattern with defer resp.Body.Close()), reading the response body with io.ReadAll, and building a simple HTTP server (http.HandleFunc, http.ListenAndServe, reading request body and query params, writing a JSON response). These are the building blocks every Go service is made from.
